correctness.rationale: For every real spectrum and d>=2, conditional Haar row uniformity gives independent Dirichlet row squared magnitudes and a Beta(1,d−2) coordinate modulus in the orthogonal complement (with Y=1 at d=2). This directly reconstructs the variance product even at scalar spectra, and beta integration yields exact positive-order moments for all k in 1..d−1 and a,b>=0 with ka+(d−k)b=1. Summing ordered entries produces the stated mean and gamma-ratio limits in each regime. Exact second moments, endpoints, and seeded samples were checked using the embedded program; finite samples are not proof.

originality.rationale: The exact general-spectrum Dirichlet-variance × independent Beta factorization and the all-rank l1 gamma formula are not stated in the primary works inspected. Directly relevant 2015 work has only l1 upper bounds; known rank-one facts are explicitly excluded from the novelty assertion; later prescribed-spectrum CLTs are not finite exact equalities. General orbital-corner and projection matrix-beta densities may yield the same marginal via integration, so an unindexed equivalent is a genuine residual risk and independent verification is not claimed.
residual_risks: Classical two-by-two Jacobi/matrix-beta density may implicitly evaluate the rank-projector off-diagonal modulus law, even if a quantum-coherence specialization is not published.
The orbital Gelfand–Tsetlin corner array has enough information to recover off-diagonal magnitudes; an explicit computation in an unindexed work may dominate the present factorization and moments.
Exact equality in distribution is not a claim of a unique generative representation or independent off-diagonal entries; source coverage cannot rule out unpublished equivalents.

value.rationale: Randomly rotated maximally mixed rank-k projectors form a canonical complex Grassmannian quantum-state family, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The exact all-rank mean l1 coherence evaluates the 2015 bounds in a motivated unsolved family; the general-spectrum factorization provides a reusable probabilistic representation. Fixed-rank, proportional-rank and fixed-corank regimes have qualitatively different linear, square-root and bounded scaling. Existing pure-state endpoints and standard probability facts are openly credited, and no unproved general-spectrum closed-form average is claimed.
